# Books

| Book | Use in the course |
|---|---|
| Cox, Doudna & O'Donnell — *Molecular Biology: Principles and Practice*, 2nd ed. (2015) | The molecular foundation. Ch. 1–8 for the opening weeks, ch. 11–22 as a reference throughout |
| Chisholm — *Theoretical Ecology: Concepts and Models with R* (2025) | Optional. Useful if you want the ecological models behind the inferences we draw |

Textbook figures shown in lectures are used for teaching under institutional
permissions and are not redistributed from this repository.

# Software

Install these before week 3. All of them are free, and all run on Linux, macOS
and Windows.

| Tool | What you need it for | Where |
|---|---|---|
| R (≥ 4.3) and RStudio | Every computational exercise | [posit.co](https://posit.co/download/rstudio-desktop/) |
| Quarto | Reports, and the slides you are reading | [quarto.org](https://quarto.org) |
| Git | Submitting seminar material to this repository | [git-scm.com](https://git-scm.com) |
| A GitHub account | Attendance, seminar registration, slide submission | [github.com](https://github.com) |

R packages used in the practicals:

```r
install.packages(c("tidyverse", "readr", "knitr", "DT", "ape", "phangorn", "vegan"))
```

::: {.callout-tip}
## Working with AI assistants

The [introduction lecture](lectures/introduction.html) covers GitHub Copilot,
Claude Code, the `btw` package, Quarto templates, and running a local model with
LM Studio when the data should not leave your machine. The
[syllabus](syllabus.qmd#responsible-use-of-ai) sets out what you must declare.
:::

# Sequence and biodiversity databases

| Database | What it holds |
|---|---|
| [NCBI GenBank / SRA](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/) | Sequences, genomes and raw reads |
| [ENA](https://www.ebi.ac.uk/ena) | The European mirror and submission route |
| [BOLD Systems](https://www.boldsystems.org/) | Curated COI barcodes with specimen metadata |
| [SILVA](https://www.arb-silva.de/) | Curated rRNA reference alignments |
| [UNITE](https://unite.ut.ee/) | Fungal ITS reference sequences, hosted at Tartu |
| [GBIF](https://www.gbif.org/) | Occurrence records, for putting molecular detections in context |
| [PR2](https://pr2-database.org/) | Protist ribosomal reference database |

# Datasets used in class

| Dataset | Used in |
|---|---|
| EEA bathing-water quality, 1990–2024 | Introduction lecture — a large real table to practise on |
| Course sequencing runs | Weeks 4–7, released as they are generated |

The EEA table is ~100 MB and is **not** stored in this repository. Download it
from the [EEA data hub](https://www.eea.europa.eu/en/datahub) and place it in
the project root under its original name; the introduction lecture reads it from
there.

# Reference material for your seminar

Choose a paper that makes a *methodological* argument, not only a biological
one — the seminar is about how the evidence was produced. Good hunting grounds:

- *Molecular Ecology* and *Molecular Ecology Resources*
- *Environmental DNA*
- *Methods in Ecology and Evolution*
- *Nucleic Acids Research* — for the method itself rather than its application

See the [seminar page](seminars/index.qmd) for how to claim one.
